verifications.claim: Gary Woodland underwent successful surgery in September 2023 to remove a benign lesion (tumor) from his brain.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "underwent surgery to remove part of a lesion from his brain in September 2023" (R1); "Surgery in September 2023... removed much of the lesion" (R2); "surgery in September of 2023 to remove a lesion... benign tumor" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm the date, success, and nature of the surgery to remove a benign brain lesion/tumor.

verifications.claim: The benign lesion (tumor) had caused fear.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "biggest issue was fear and anxiety" (R1); "lesion on the part of his brain that caused unfounded fears" (R2); "lesion was on the part of the brain that controls Woodland's fear and anxiety" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state the lesion caused fear and anxiety symptoms pre-surgery.

verifications.claim: The benign lesion (tumor) had later caused severe PTSD.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: "post-traumatic stress disorder as a result of the brain surgery" (R1); "PTSD... following brain surgery" (R2); "PTSD symptoms that were lingering effects from the lesion and the surgery" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: PTSD is attributed to the surgery/trauma, not directly caused by the lesion later; lesion caused pre-surgery symptoms.

verifications.claim: The procedure involved removing a baseball-sized portion of the tumor.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "baseball-sized hole cut... removed much of the lesion" (R2); "drill a hole in his skull the size of a baseball to remove most of the lesion" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe drilling a baseball-sized hole to remove most/much of the lesion, directly matching the claim.

verifications.claim: Gary Woodland returned to the PGA Tour in January 2024.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "returned to the Tour months later" after Sept 2023 (R1); "His return in January 2024" (R2); "returned to the PGA Tour in January of 2024" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state return in January 2024.

verifications.claim: Surgeons performed a craniotomy to remove a tumor that was causing neurological symptoms, such as fear and seizures.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "small seizures at night... fear and anxiety" (R1); "lesion... caused unfounded fears... seizures" implied; "drill a hole... lesion that controls fear" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe skull surgery matching craniotomy, lesion/tumor causing fear, anxiety, seizures; term 'craniotomy' not used but procedure matches precisely.

verifications.claim: Gary Woodland struggled significantly with anxiety following the surgery.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: "PTSD... hypervigilant... struggled... crying" post-surgery (R1); fear gone post-surgery but PTSD symptoms include anxiety-like issues (R2)
verifications.reasoning: Post-surgery struggles are PTSD (anxiety-related), but sources specify fear gone after surgery; anxiety not directly named post-surgery.

verifications.claim: Gary Woodland struggled significantly with PTSD following the surgery.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "brain surgery that led to a PTSD diagnosis" (R1); "hurting badly with PTSD" post-surgery (R2); "overcomes tumor removal, PTSD" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: All sources directly confirm significant PTSD struggles following surgery.

verifications.claim: Gary Woodland revealed in early 2026 that he often felt like he was "dying" during his recovery.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "two weeks ago... 'inside, I feel like I’m dying'" (interview pre-March 2026 win) (R2); same quote (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Direct quote from early 2026 interview about feeling like dying during recovery/PTSD.

verifications.claim: Gary Woodland revealed in early 2026 that he was living in fear during his recovery.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: Early 2026 reveal quotes 'feel like I’m dying,' not 'living in fear'; fear explicitly gone post-surgery.

verifications.claim: Gary Woodland won the 2026 Texas Children’s Houston Open.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "won... Texas Children's Houston Open" March 29, 2026 (all sources)
verifications.reasoning: All sources directly report the 2026 win.

verifications.claim: The 2026 Texas Children’s Houston Open was Gary Woodland's first PGA Tour event win since the surgery.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "first PGA Tour win after brain surgery"... since 2019 U.S. Open (post-2023 surgery)" (R1); "first title since brain surgery" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm first PGA Tour win since surgery (and since 2019).

verifications.claim: Gary Woodland made his return to competitive golf at the Sony Open in January 2024
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm January 2024 PGA Tour return but do not specify Sony Open.
